newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia army uncovers major rebel ambush plan.
newsitem.headline: Colombia army uncovers major rebel ambush plan.

text.p: Colombia's military said on Tuesday it had frustrated plans by leftist rebels to stage a major attack on the outskirts of the capital in which scores of soldiers might have been killed.

Gen. Euclides Sanchez said the planned attack by the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) was to have been carried out in reprisal for the dismantling this week of four rebel camps in a mountainous area southwest of Bogota.

Sanchez said the 80 troops in the counterinsurgency operation were ordered back to the capital on Monday. But before they returned military intelligence officials discovered about 220 pounds (100 kg) of dynamite alongside a stretch of rural highway where their convoy was due to pass.

The dynamite, set to be detonated by remote control, was hidden in 10 plastic containers placed along 1,640 feet (500 meters) of the highway, Sanchez told Reuters. He did not elaborate, but more than 30 soliders were killed by the FARC last year when a highway laden with dynamite in southwest Narino province exploded.

In other developments, police and military officials said five small bombs placed by suspected National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels in strategic locations around Cali, Colombia's second city, were deactivated by authorities early on Tuesday.

The Marxist-led FARC and ELN have been waging war against the state since the mid-1960s. But groups have rejected recent peace overtures from the government of President Ernesto Samper, whom they dismiss as "illegitimate" because of charges that he used drug money to finance his 1994 election campaign.
